must_fix.title: Changelog entry is under 8.5.1 but the docstring says versionadded 8.6
must_fix.evidence: CHANGES.md adds the Duration entry at the end of '## Version 8.5.1 / Unreleased' (after the {pr}`3865` entry), while src/click/types.py:675 says '.. versionadded:: 8.6'. New 8.6 features such as Parameter.spec are listed under '## Version 8.6.0', and the repo writes the full version in versionadded (core.py:115, 2548, 3938 use '.. versionadded:: 8.6.0'). Move the entry to 8.6.0 and use 8.6.0 in the docstring.

nits: Bounds or timedelta values below a millisecond give confusing messages because _format_duration truncates: Duration(max=timedelta(microseconds=1500)).convert(timedelta(microseconds=1700)) -> '1ms is not in the range x<=1ms.'
show_default renders a timedelta default as '0:05:00', which Duration cannot parse; '5m' would be clearer.
Plain pyright reports 4 new errors at types.py:621/624 (fullmatch called with Any|bool); the repo's typing run only uses --verifytypes, but an isinstance(value, str) check would fix it.
Changelog entry lacks the {pr}/{issue} reference every other entry has.
The core.py range-help change also lets count=True with Duration produce a timedelta; harmless but untested.

report:
I wouldn't merge this yet: there's one thing the contributor must fix. Everything the issue requires passes: `.venv/bin/pytest` (2355 passed), `.venv/bin/mypy` ("Success: no issues found"), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.

The parsing and error handling hold up. None of these cases crashed: `999999999d24h` (overflows `timedelta`), 5000-digit numbers, `b"5s"`, `None`, booleans, floats, non-ASCII digits, units in the wrong order or repeated, and leading or trailing whitespace. Each one gives a normal usage error and exit code 2. Negative values are rejected, the inclusive bounds behave correctly, and the type is exported from both `click` and `click.types`. The help text shows the range, e.g. `[default: 0:05:00; x>=1s]`.

**Must fix: the changelog entry is under the wrong version.**
- The `Duration` entry was added at the bottom of `## Version 8.5.1 / Unreleased` in `CHANGES.md`, after the `{pr}3865` entry. But the docstring at `src/click/types.py:675` says `.. versionadded:: 8.6`.
- `CHANGES.md` has two unreleased sections. A new public type belongs under `## Version 8.6.0`, where the other new 8.6 APIs such as `Parameter.spec` are listed.
- The repo also writes the full version in `versionadded`, for example `.. versionadded:: 8.6.0` at `core.py:115`, 2548 and 3938. The docstring should match.

**Nits:**
- **Sub-millisecond bounds give a confusing error.** Formatting drops anything below a millisecond, so `Duration(max=timedelta(microseconds=1500)).convert(timedelta(microseconds=1700), None, None)` fails with "1ms is not in the range x<=1ms."
- **The default is shown in the wrong syntax.** With `show_default`, a `timedelta` default is shown as `0:05:00`, which `Duration` itself can't parse. Showing `5m` would be clearer.
- **New pyright errors.** Plain `.venv/bin/pyright` reports four new errors in `types.py` at lines 621 and 624: `fullmatch` is given an `Any | bool` value. The repo's typing run only uses `pyright --verifytypes`, so this doesn't block the merge, but an `isinstance(value, str)` check would fix it.
- **No PR reference in the changelog.** The new entry has no `{pr}`/`{issue}` link, though every other entry has one.
- **Odd result with `count=True`.** Because of the `core.py` change, `--c --c` with `type=click.Duration(), count=True` gives `timedelta(seconds=2)`. It's harmless, but it isn't covered.

My `git stash` probe failed before changing anything, and `git status` is the same as when I started. Scratch files are in a `mktemp -d` directory outside the repo.
